conventions.convention: δ_h^i u(x)=(u(x+he_i)-u(x))/h on Ω∩(Ω-he_i), whereas τ_h u(x)=u(x-h); the forward shift is τ_{-he_i}.
Local solutions here belong to H¹(Ω), have L²_loc forcing, and satisfy compact-test identities. The form is linear in the solution and conjugate-linear in the test.
The quotient converse requires 1<p<∞. Forward coordinate estimates include p=1 and p=∞; the Euclidean-vector estimate has factor n^{|1/p-1/2|}.
Global H² regularity requires a bounded C² domain, W^{1,∞} principal coefficients, bounded lower-order coefficients and zero Dirichlet data. Its estimate retains the L² solution term.
Higher boundary regularity uses C^{k+2} boundary, W^{k+1,∞} principal coefficients, W^{k,∞} lower-order coefficients and H^k forcing.
Subsolutions use a(u,φ)≤∫fφ for nonnegative real tests. Order theory concerns real coefficients and classes; boundary order is expressed by positive-part membership in H¹₀.
De Giorgi and Harnack results use the scalar principal operator with measurable symmetric coefficients satisfying θI≤A≤M_a²I.
Weak Harnack requires B_{2R} compactly contained in the domain, q>n/2 forcing, and 0<p<n/(n-2) for n≥3; every finite positive p is allowed for n=2. Forcing enters as R^{2-n/q}‖F‖.
Primitive ideals are annihilators of arbitrary nonzero simple unital left modules; highest-weight realization is not part of the definition.
The PBW filtration starts at degree zero with F_{-1}=0; the associated variety is the classical zero locus of gr I in g*, including the empty variety for I=U(g).
Central-character weight orbits use the dot action w·λ=w(λ+ρ)-ρ.
The normalized sl₂ Casimir is Ω=ef+fe+h²/2=4C, where C is the Killing-form Casimir; its eigenvalue at highest weight λ(h)=λ is λ(λ+2)/2.

load_bearing.statement: Under Countable Choice, forward coordinate quotient bounds hold for W^{1,p} classes, 1≤p≤∞, on valid contained segments. Uniform local coordinate quotient bounds for an L^p class, 1<p<∞, give W^{1,p} membership and weak convergence to the derivatives; tangential half-space quotients converge strongly for p<∞.

Assume Countable Choice. For uniformly elliptic L with W^{1,∞} principal coefficients and bounded lower-order coefficients, an H¹(Ω) local weak solution with f∈L²_loc(Ω) belongs to H²_loc(Ω), with ‖u‖_{H²(Ω′)}≤C(‖f‖_{L²(Ω″)}+‖u‖_{L²(Ω″)}) whenever Ω′⊂⊂Ω″⊂⊂Ω.

Assume Countable Choice. δ_h^i(ηu)-ηδ_h^iu=(δ_h^iη)τ_{-he_i}u on the shrunken domain, with L^p norm at most ‖Dη‖∞‖u‖p. The item also proves the W^{m,∞}/H^m multiplier rule and compact-support membership in H^m₀.

Assume Countable Choice. On a bounded C² domain in dimension n≥2, a zero-Dirichlet weak solution for uniformly elliptic L with W^{1,∞} principal coefficients, bounded lower-order coefficients and L² forcing lies in H², with ‖u‖_{H²}≤C(‖f‖₂+‖u‖₂).

Assume Countable Choice and AC. For real u∈H¹, (u-k)^± are locally H¹ with the stated level-set gradient formulas; global membership requires L² membership, automatically available on finite-measure domains. Compact cutoff products lie in H¹₀; admissibility requires the stated continuous source pairing.

Assume Countable Choice and AC. For n≥2 and measurable symmetric θI≤A≤M_a²I, every nonnegative H¹ homogeneous weak subsolution satisfies ess sup_{B_{ρR}}u≤C(avg_{B_R}u^p)^{1/p} for every p>0 and 0<ρ<1, with scale-independent C(n,θ,M_a,ρ,p).

Under Countable Choice and AC, positive homogeneous scalar supersolutions satisfy the reciprocal negative-moment bound for every p>0 and a comparison of opposite p₀ moments on B_{3R/4}, for some p₀ depending only on n,θ,M_a, without assuming a positive lower bound.

Let A be a unital complex algebra admitting a countable complex basis and M a simple left A-module. Then End_A(M)=C·id_M; consequently Z(A) acts by a unital complex-algebra character. This applies to U(g) for finite-dimensional complex g.

Assume AC. For sl₂, U_χ is simple iff χ is not the central character of any nonzero finite-dimensional module, equivalently χ(Ω)≠n(n+2)/2 for every integer n≥0. In this case every nonzero U_χ-module is faithful, every Verma module over χ is simple, and its annihilator is U(g)kerχ.

concerns.concern: The Definition says its L²_loc-data notion is 'strictly weaker than the Dirichlet notion ... which asks for u∈H¹₀(Ω) and a datum in the dual of H¹₀'. As an unrestricted comparison this is inaccurate: H⁻¹ Dirichlet data need not be locally L², so a general Dirichlet solution need not meet this local definition's data hypothesis. For example, an interval Dirichlet solution with point-mass forcing has H⁻¹ forcing but no L²_loc forcing. The comparison should be restricted to the common L²_loc-data setting. The actual definition and its stated test-space equivalences are unaffected.

seams_checked.note: The no-kernel-term corollary uses the opened L² Fredholm and bounded-solution-map statements under AC and Countable Choice; it retains the fixed inverse norm. Eigenfunction bootstrapping uses the exact zero-trace weak-eigenpair identity. Smooth-test density is used within its L² scope.

The actual item citation is the Hölder-space/scaled-norm definition in the De Giorgi–Nash theorem. Its local Hölder representative and seminorm use agrees with that definition; no Schauder estimate is applied to merely measurable coefficients.

Opened cor-minimisers-are-classical-when-elliptic-regularity-applies. Its smooth case assumes a bounded C∞ domain, forcing smooth near the closure and a smooth boundary lift G. It subtracts G, proves zero trace and forcing f+ΔG, then applies the zero-boundary classical-solution corollary.

Opened the obstacle definition, admissible-set lemma and Lewy–Stampacchia theorem. The trace/positive-part equivalence is used only for n≥2 bounded C¹ domains, with a separate interval supplier for n=1. The Lewy–Stampacchia F4/F10 clauses preserve the truncation supplier's source-continuity conditions and supply a bounded H⁻¹ reaction functional.
